mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted, {ذكر رَحْمَة رَبك}: al-Farrāʾ said it is nominative by كهيعص, and al-Zajjāj objected to that against him. Al-Akhfash said: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "among what is narrated to you is the mention of the mercy of your Lord" (فِيمَا يقص عَلَيْك ذكر رَحْمَة رَبك).
And it is said that its implied form is "this which is recited is the mention of the mercy of your Lord" (هَذَا الَّذِي يُتْلَى ذكر رَحْمَة رَبك), and the underlying arrangement of the speech is "your Lord's mentioning of His servant Zakariyyā with mercy" (ذكر رَبك عَبده زَكَرِيَّا برحمة).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {إِذْ نَادَى ربه}: the governing word (ʿāmil) of إِذْ is ذكر.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying {شيبا}: accusative as an explanation (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz (specification)); and it is said to be the maṣdar (verbal noun) of شَاب شيبا.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying {يَرِثنِي وَيَرِث}: whoever reads it in the jussive (jazm) makes it the answer to the request, because the request is like the imperative in its ruling. Whoever reads it in the nominative makes it a naʿt (adjective) of الْوَليّ, or [takes it] as a break (qaṭʿ, a new sentence). Its implied form, if you make it an adjective, is "so grant me from Yourself an heir inheriting my knowledge and my prophethood" (فَهَب لي من لَدُنْك وليا وَارِثا علمي ونبوتي).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying {من الْكبر عتيا}: it is accusative by بلغت, its implied form being "an extreme age" (سنا عتيا). Its origin is عُتُوّ, the maṣdar (verbal noun) of عتا يعتو; they replaced the wāw with a yāʾ and the ḍamma before it with a kasra so that the yāʾ would be sound, because that is lighter, and so that the verse-endings would agree. It has also been read with kasra on the ʿayn (عِتيا), so that the kasra follows the kasra.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {سويا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent (muḍmar) pronoun in تكلم, or a naʿt (adjective) of ثلاث لَيَال; and likewise بشرا.

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying {وَآتَيْنَاهُ الحكم صَبيا}: صَبيا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying {مَكَانا قصيا}: an adverb (ẓarf); and it is said to be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) on the implied form "so she made for a distant place with him" (فقصدت بِهِ مَكَانا قصيا).

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying {فناداها من تحتهَا}: whoever reads the mīm of مِن with kasra (the preposition), the pronoun in فناداها is the pronoun of ʿĪsā (peace be upon him), i.e. "so ʿĪsā called her from beneath her", i.e. from beneath her garments. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to Jibrīl (peace be upon him), and the implied form is "so Jibrīl called her from below her", i.e. from a place lower than her position — as you say "my house is beneath your house", i.e. lower than your house, and "my town is beneath your town", i.e. lower than it; and as He said of Paradise تجْرِي من تحتهَا الْأَنْهَار ("rivers flow beneath it"), i.e. from below it.
So تحت is meant here as the direction facing the thing; thus Jibrīl (peace be upon him) spoke to her from the direction facing her, not from below her. And if the pronoun is for ʿĪsā (peace be upon him), تحت means "below", because the place where ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) was born was below her. What shows that ٤ [Translator's note: a stray numeral, apparently a page marker, stands here in the source] تحت can mean the direction facing a thing is His saying {قد جعل رَبك تَحْتك سريا}, i.e. in the place facing you, not that it was below her. As for reading the mīm of مَن with fatḥa (the relative noun), he makes مَن the fāʿil (agent), and there is then no agent pronoun in فناداها; and مَن in this reading is ʿĪsā (peace be upon him), because he is the one who was below her, so مَن occurs here for a specific referent, though its basic use is for generality. It has also been said that مَن refers to Jibrīl (peace be upon him), as in the first [reading].

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying {تساقط عَلَيْك رطبا}: رطبا is accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz (specification)); and it is said to be the object of هزي. This is only so on the reading of whoever reads it with tāʾ and without doubling, or with doubling, or with fatḥa on the tāʾ and doubling; and in تساقط is the pronoun of the palm tree (النَّخْلَة). It may also be the pronoun of the trunk (الْجذع) — this on the reading of whoever reads it with tāʾ — as they said ذهبت بعض أَصَابِعه ("some of his fingers went", with a feminine verb for a masculine subject annexed to a feminine). As for whoever reads it with yāʾ, there can be in يساقط only the pronoun of the trunk. As for whoever reads it with ḍamma on the tāʾ, without doubling and with kasra on the qāf (تُساقِط), رطبا is the object of تساقط; and it is said to be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with the object implied, its implied form being "its fruit will fall upon you as fresh dates" (تساقط ثَمَرهَا عَلَيْك رطبا). جنيا is a naʿt (adjective). The palm tree indicates the fruit, so its omission is good. And the bāʾ in بجذع is redundant (zāʾida).

mekki-muskil:26-26.t:
His saying {وقري عينا}: accusative as an explanation (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz (specification)).
His saying {فإمَّا تَرين}: its pattern originally is تفعلين, like تضربين, and the original form of the word is ترأيين. The vowel of the hamza was thrown onto the rāʾ, as is done in ترى; then the vowelled yāʾ, which is the third radical (lām al-fiʿl), was replaced by an alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa; then the alif was dropped because it was quiescent and the yāʾ of the feminine after it was quiescent, so تَرين remained. Then the doubled nūn of emphasis entered, so the nūn of inflection was dropped because of the verb becoming indeclinable (bināʾ), and the yāʾ was given kasra because it was quiescent and the first [element] of the doubled nūn was quiescent. The yāʾ was not dropped, since there is no kasra before it to indicate it, and because the third radical before it had already been dropped. So it became تَرين as it is in the recitation [Translator's note: i.e. تَرَيِنَّ]. So understand that.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t:
His saying {أمك بغيا}: the origin of بغيا is بغوي, so it is on the pattern فعول; but the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ, and the ghayn was given kasra because it adjoins the two yāʾs and so that the quiescent yāʾ would be sound. فعول here has the meaning of فاعلة (active participle), and for that reason it came without a hāʾ [of the feminine] while it is an adjective of a feminine — just as فعول comes without hāʾ for the feminine when it has the meaning of مفعول (passive participle), as in His saying, the Exalted, {فَمِنْهَا ركوبهم}. بغيا is not originally on the pattern فعيل; had it been فعيل, the hāʾ would have been required for the feminine, because فعيل, when it is for the feminine with the meaning of فاعل, requires the hāʾ, as in their saying امْرَأَة رحيمة and عليمة with the meaning of راحمة and عالمة. Since بغي came without hāʾ, it is known that it is فعول and not فعيل.
His saying {يَا أُخْت هَارُون}: the tāʾ in أُخْت is not radical, but it stands in the position of a radical, because it was added for ilḥāq (assimilation to a pattern). For the original of the noun is أخوة on the pattern فعلة; the wāw was dropped and the hamza given ḍamma to indicate the dropped wāw, just as the bāʾ in بنت was given kasra to indicate the dropped yāʾ — the origin of بنت being بنية. So the noun remained on two letters, the hamza and the khāʾ; then the tāʾ was added and it was assimilated to the pattern فُعْل. The diminutive and the plural indicate what we have said, because you restore it to its origin in the diminutive and the plural, saying أخية and أخوات. The dropping of the wāw in it is not according to analogy; and it is said: because of frequent use. Analogy would have been to say in the singular أخاة, changing the wāw into an alif because it is vowelled and the letter before it has fatḥa. Likewise the tāʾ in بنت was added to assimilate the noun to the pattern جِذْع, because its yāʾ was dropped not according to analogy; except that in بنت the yāʾ is not restored in the plural, but it is restored in the diminutive: you say in the diminutive بنية, as you say in أخت أَخِيه [Translator's note: so in the source; the expected diminutive is أُخَيَّة], and you say in the plural بَنَات, and you do not say بنيات as you say أَخَوَات.

mekki-muskil:29-29.t: His saying من كَانَ فِي المهد صَبيا: صَبيا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and كَانَ is redundant (zāʾida), and the governing word (ʿāmil) of the ḥāl is the [implied] being-settled (al-istiqrār). It is also said that كَانَ here means "occurred / came to be", and in it is its noun as a latent (muḍmar) pronoun, and صَبيا is likewise a ḥāl, its governor being نُكَلِّم; and it is said: كَانَ [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off thus in the source]. Al-Zajjāj said: مَن is for condition (sharṭ), and the meaning is "whoever is in the cradle as a child, how shall we speak to him?"

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying {مَا دمت حَيا}: مَا is in the position of the accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "for the time my life lasts"; and it is said to be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). حَيا is the khabar of دمت, and the tāʾ is the noun of دَامَ, because دَامَ is one of the sisters of kāna.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t: His saying {وَبرا بوالدتي}: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to مُبَارَكًا, and مبارك is the second object of جعل. Whoever reads برا in the genitive conjoins it to الصَّلَاة.

mekki-muskil:34-34.t: His saying {قَول الْحق}: whoever reads قول in the nominative implies a mubtadaʾ (subject) and makes قَول الْحق its khabar (predicate), its implied form being "That is ʿĪsā son of Maryam; that is the word of truth" (ذَلِك عِيسَى بن مَرْيَم ذَلِك قَول الْحق), or "this speech is the word of truth". And it is said that the implied pronoun هُوَ is an allusion to ʿĪsā (peace be upon him), because he came into being by the word of Allah (exalted be His mention), and Allah named him a "word" since by the word he came to be; for that reason al-Kisāʾī said, according to this meaning, that قَول الْحق is a naʿt (adjective) of ʿĪsā (peace be upon him). Whoever reads قولا in the accusative takes it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "I say the word of truth".

mekki-muskil:36-36.t: His saying {وَإِن الله رَبِّي}: whoever reads أَن with fatḥa conjoins it to الصَّلَاة, and whoever reads it with kasra begins a new sentence with it.

mekki-muskil:41-41.t: His saying {إِنَّه كَانَ صديقا نَبيا}: صديق is the khabar of كَانَ, and نبي is a naʿt (adjective) of صديق; and it is said to be a khabar after a khabar.

mekki-muskil:46-46.t: His saying {أراغب أَنْت عَن آلهتي}: رَاغِب is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and أَنْت is nominative by its verbal sense, which is "desiring", and it stands in place of the khabar (predicate). Beginning with an indefinite noun is good because it leans on the interrogative alif before it.

mekki-muskil:47-47.t: His saying {قَالَ سَلام عَلَيْك}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition with its genitive noun is its khabar (predicate). Beginning with an indefinite noun is good here because it carries the meaning of the accusative [i.e. a supplication], and it also carries the meaning of disavowal and parting; so since it conveys benefits, beginning with it is permitted. The rule is that one does not begin with an indefinite noun unless it conveys a benefit to the one addressed.

mekki-muskil:52-52.t: His saying {وقربناه نجيا}: نجيا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:55-55.t: His saying {مرضيا}: its origin is مرضو on the pattern مفعول, and it is from the roots with wāw, because of their saying الرضْوَان. Then they replaced the wāw with a yāʾ and gave kasra to what precedes it so that the quiescent yāʾ would be sound, and because it is lighter than the wāw.

mekki-muskil:58-58.t: His saying {خروا سجدا وبكيا}: both are accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial), and بكيا is then the plural of باك. It is also said that بكيا is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) and is not the plural of باك, its implied form being "they fell down prostrating and wept a weeping" (خروا سجدا وَبكوا بكيا). Its origin in both views is بكويا on the pattern فعول; then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ and what precedes it given kasra so that the quiescence of the yāʾ would be sound, and because it is lighter. A group of the readers gave kasra to the bāʾ [Translator's note: the source says "the yāʾ"; the reading meant is بِكِيًّا with kasra on the bāʾ] so that kasra follows kasra and so that it is lighter for the work of the tongue.

mekki-muskil:62-62.t: His saying {إِلَّا سَلاما}: accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); and it is said to be a badal (substitute) from لَغْو.

mekki-muskil:63-63.t: His saying {تِلْكَ الْجنَّة الَّتِي نورث من عبادنَا من كَانَ تقيا}: نورث takes two objects because it is a four-letter verb from أورث. The first object is a hāʾ omitted from the ṣila (relative clause) of الَّتِي because of the length of the noun, its implied form being نورثها; and the second object is مَن in His saying من كَانَ تقيا. And مِن is attached to (mutaʿalliq) نورث or to تقي, and the implied form is "That is the Paradise which We give as inheritance to whoever is God-fearing among Our servants" (تِلْكَ الْجنَّة الَّتِي نورثها من كَانَ تقيا من عبادنَا).

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying {قَالَ كَذَلِك}: the kāf is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "he said: the matter is thus" (قَالَ الْأَمر كَذَلِك); so it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).

mekki-muskil:69-69.t:
His saying {أَيهمْ أَشد على الرَّحْمَن عتيا}: Hārūn the Reader read أَيهمْ in the accusative, making لننزعن govern it. The nominative in أَيهمْ, according to al-Khalīl, is by way of ḥikāya (reported speech): so it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) is أَشد, the implied form being "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect the one of whom, because of his insolence, it is said: which of these is most insolent?" (ثمَّ لننزعن من كل شيعَة الَّذِي من أجل عتوه يُقَال أَي هَؤُلَاءِ أَشد عتيا). This is like the poet's saying:
... فأبيت لَا حرج وَلَا محروم ...
(And I spent the night neither constrained nor deprived.)
i.e. in the state of one of whom it is said: "neither constrained nor deprived". According to Sībawayh this is nominative by لا, because it is like ليس, and the khabar of ليس is omitted, its implied form being "no one constrained and no one deprived is in my place" (لَا حرج وَلَا محروم فِي مَكَاني); and the yāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the reference is to the first-person tāʾ of فأبيت] refers back to the noun of بات, and the clause is the khabar of بات. Whoever makes it ḥikāya makes the reported clause the khabar of بات, and the hāʾ in the implied لَهُ refers back to الَّذِي.
Yūnus held that أي is nominative as a mubtadaʾ by way of ḥikāya, and that the verb, namely لننزعن, is suspended (taʿlīq) so that it does not govern it in its outward form. But according to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl a verb like لننزعن may not be suspended; only verbs such as the verbs of doubt and the like, whose occurrence is not realised, may be suspended.
Sībawayh held that أيا is indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, because for him it is in the position of الَّذِي and مَا; but it differs from them in that annexation (iḍāfa) is permitted in it, so it was made declinable since annexation is permitted in it. Then, when what refers back to it was omitted from its ṣila (relative clause), it was weakened and returned to its origin, which is indeclinability, like الَّذِي and مَا. Had you made the pronoun overt, indeclinability would not be permitted according to him. The implied form of the speech, according to him, is "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect whichever of them is most…" (ثمَّ لننزعن من كل شيعَة أَيهمْ هُوَ أَشد), as you say "We shall surely draw out the one who is most…" (لننزعن الَّذِي هُوَ أَشد). Omitting هُوَ with الَّذِي is ugly; and it has been read تَمامًا على الَّذِي أحسن with أحسن in the nominative on the assumption that هُوَ is omitted — and the omission with الَّذِي is ugly, while with أي it is good. So since أي differs from its sisters, omission with it is good; and when هُوَ was omitted, أيا was made indeclinable on ḍamma.
Sībawayh has been objected to in his view, and it was said: how can an annexed noun (muḍāf) be made indeclinable when it is fully declinable (mutamakkin)? And there is room for consideration in this. Had the omitted pronoun appeared with أي, there would be nothing in أي but the accusative, according to all.
Al-Kisāʾī said: لننزعن falls upon the meaning. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning of لننزعن is "We shall surely call out", so it does not govern, because it has the meaning of calling. Some of the Kufans said: لننزعن does not govern أَيهمْ only because in it is the meaning of condition and requital, so what precedes it does not govern it; the meaning is "We shall surely draw out from every group, whether they supported one another or did not", as you say ضربت الْقَوْم أَيهمْ غضب ("I struck the people, whichever of them got angry"), the meaning being "whether they got angry or did not". And from al-Mubarrad: أَيهمْ is nominative because it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) شيعة, and the meaning is "from those who sided together [to see] which of them…", i.e. from those who helped one another and looked to see which of them [was most insolent].

mekki-muskil:72-72.t: His saying {فِيهَا جثيا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) if you make it the plural of جاث, and accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) if you do not make it a plural but make it a maṣdar. Its origin in both views is جثوو on the pattern فعول; then the wāw was assimilated into the wāw, and the word became heavy with two ḍammas and two final wāws, so they replaced the wāw with a yāʾ and gave kasra to what precedes it so that the quiescent yāʾ would be sound, and because it is lighter. A group of the readers read it with kasra on the jīm by way of harmony (itbāʿ), for lightness and congruence.

mekki-muskil:75-75.t: His saying {إِمَّا الْعَذَاب وَإِمَّا السَّاعَة}: both are accusative as a badal (substitute) from مَا in His saying {حَتَّى إِذا رَأَوْا مَا يوعدون}.

mekki-muskil:80-80.t:
His saying {ونرثه مَا يَقُول}: the preposition is omitted, its implied form being "and We shall inherit from him what he speaks of" (ونرث مِنْهُ مَا يَقُول), i.e. We shall inherit from him his wealth and his children.
And His saying {ويأتينا فَردا}: a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:87-87.t: His saying {إِلَّا من اتخذ عِنْد الرَّحْمَن}: مَن is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the latent nominative pronoun in يملكُونَ. It may also be in the position of the accusative as an exception, on the basis that it is not of the same kind as the first [i.e. a disconnected exception].

mekki-muskil:90-90.t: His saying {وتخر الْجبَال هدا}: هدا is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:91-91.t: His saying {أَن دعوا للرحمن ولدا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:92-92.t: His saying {للرحمن أَن يتَّخذ ولدا}: أَن is in the position of the nominative by يَنْبَغِي.

mekki-muskil:93-93.t: His saying {إِن كل من}: إِن has the meaning of مَا (negation). كل is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is إلا آتي الرَّحْمَن. آتي is an active participle, and الرحمن is in the position of the accusative by the [participle of] coming. عبدا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and likewise فَردا.
